about.origins.title: Supporting Global Hatcheries Since 2017
about.origins.p1: Founded with a vision to standardize high-performance inputs, VARS Aquaculture has evolved from a local trial in Türkiye to a multi-national entity. We provide the critical link between resource-rich origins and high-demand markets across South Korea, the Middle East and Canada.
about.origins.p2: Since 2017, VARS Aquaculture has supported hatcheries with high-performance live feed and nutritional solutions designed to improve reliability, increase yields and drive measurable results.
about.origins.p3: What began with targeted rotifer trials in Türkiye has evolved into a growing network of trusted customers and references across South Korea, the Middle East, Canada and beyond. Today, we have had the opportunity to serve and power hatchery systems across species and environments — backed by real-world performance data and continuous on-site support.

solutions.roadmap.title: Facilitating the Investor Journey
solutions.roadmap.description: Launching an aquaculture venture requires biological precision and technology alignment. As your expert consultants and facilitators, we guide you through every phase from feasibility to commercial operations.
solutions.roadmap.item1.title: Market Feasibility & Species Strategy
solutions.roadmap.item1.desc: Comprehensive market analysis, site viability assessment, water quality evaluation, and species selection tailored to target regional demand (EU, GCC, Asia).
solutions.roadmap.item2.title: Hatchery & RAS Engineering Design
solutions.roadmap.item2.desc: Production planning and bio-engineering for land-based Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), flow-through hatcheries, and sea-cage installations.

solutions.roadmap.item3.desc: Leveraging our direct network of leading equipment manufacturers, feed producers, genetics labs, and biosecurity vendors for optimal CAPEX/OPEX efficiency.

solutions.roadmap.item5.title: Operational Launch & Staff Training
solutions.roadmap.item5.desc: On-site commissioning, live feed (Artemia & Rotifer) culture setup, biosecurity protocol implementation, and ongoing technical advisory.
solutions.troubleshooting.title: Operational Optimization & Troubleshooting
solutions.troubleshooting.description: Facing live feed crashes, high FCR, or biosecurity bottlenecks? Our senior specialists conduct on-site and remote audits to resolve issues across the board.
solutions.troubleshooting.item1.title: FCR & Growth Audit
solutions.troubleshooting.item1.desc: Analyzing feed conversion ratios, ingredient digestibility, and feeding schedules to reduce operating costs and accelerate harvest weight.
solutions.troubleshooting.item2.title: Live Feed Crash Prevention
solutions.troubleshooting.item2.desc: Troubleshooting rotifer and Chlorella culture instability, optimizing Artemia hatch-out rates, and implementing sterile culture protocols.
solutions.troubleshooting.item3.title: Biosecurity & Pathogen Control
solutions.troubleshooting.item3.desc: Designing SPF pathogen-free barriers, water filtration protocols, and disease outbreak recovery plans for commercial hatcheries.

solutions.troubleshooting.item4.desc: Auditing packing plants and cold-chain logistics to meet European Union and GCC food safety, TRACES, and customs entry requirements.

guideIncubation.parameters.items.salinit: Use natural seawater or synthetic sea salt. Low salinity prolongs hatching time.
guideIncubation.parameters.items.tempera: Maintain constant temperature. Temperatures below 25 °C drastically decrease hatch-out velocity.
guideIncubation.parameters.items.aeratio: Keep cysts in continuous suspension. Avoid dead zones where cysts settle.
guideIncubation.parameters.items.light.d: Light triggers the embryonic development mechanism during the first 2 hours of hydration.
guideIncubation.steps.items.step1.title: Disinfection & Pre-hydration
guideIncubation.steps.items.step1.desc: Pre-soak dry Artemia cysts in clean freshwater for 30 minutes at 20–25 °C before transferring to salt water.
guideIncubation.steps.items.step2.title: Conical Tank Incubation
guideIncubation.steps.items.step2.desc: Fill conical hatching vessel with 30 ppt saltwater. Add cysts at a maximum density of 2 grams per liter.
guideIncubation.steps.items.step3.title: Harvesting & Separation
guideIncubation.steps.items.step3.desc: Turn off aeration after 20–24 hours. Nauplii swim toward light at the bottom while empty shells float to top.
guideIncubation.steps.items.step4.title: Cold-Storage Enrichment
guideIncubation.steps.items.step4.desc: Rinse harvested nauplii thoroughly. Store in chilled seawater (4–6 °C) or enrich with Emerald Chlorella.
guideIncubation.hero.title: Artemia Cysts Hatching & Incubation Manual
guideIncubation.hero.description: A step-by-step scientific guide to achieving ≥ 85% hatch-out rates, maximum nauplii biomass, and clean separation for marine larvae.
guideDecap.comparison.rows.shell.standar: Present — hatch before feeding to very young fry
guideDecap.comparison.rows.energy.standa: Standard caloric density; some energy used during hatching
guideDecap.comparison.rows.energy.decap: Higher net caloric density (502 kcal/100g) — no hatching energy loss
guideDecap.comparison.rows.equipment.dec: No hatching setup required — feed directly from the can
guideDecap.comparison.rows.biosecurity.s: Unhatched shells should be separated from feed for very sensitive fry
guideDecap.comparison.rows.biosecurity.d: No shell present — no separation step needed
guideDecap.segments.items.hatcheries.des: Operations with established hatching infrastructure often use Standard Cysts as a cost-effective live feed. For very young or sensitive post-larvae (sea bass, sea bream, grouper, shrimp), many hatcheries switch to Decapsulated Artemia to skip the hatching step and reduce shell-handling labor.
guideDecap.segments.items.aquariums.desc: Decapsulated Artemia gives a ready-to-feed, high-energy option for delicate filter feeders, seahorses, and pipefish, while Standard Cysts suit exhibits where on-site hatching is already part of the routine.
guideDecap.segments.items.retail.title: Aquarium Shops & Wholesale Retailers
guideDecap.segments.items.retail.desc: Both formats are available in shelf-stable retail cans (500g / 1kg) — Standard Cysts for customers who hatch their own live feed, and Decapsulated Artemia for customers who want a direct-feed option.
guideDecap.segments.items.hobbyists.desc: Decapsulated Artemia is convenient for direct feeding into reef tanks and fry-rearing setups without a hatching station, while Standard Cysts suit hobbyists who prefer to hatch their own nauplii.
guideDecap.hero.title: Standard vs Decapsulated Artemia Cysts: Choosing the Right Form
guideDecap.hero.description: Compare shell-on Standard Artemia Cysts and shell-free Decapsulated Artemia to find the right fit for your hatching setup, feeding protocol, and customer segment.
guideDecap.intro.heading: Standard vs Decapsulated Artemia: What's the Difference?
guideDecap.intro.paragraph1: Artemia cysts naturally have a thick outer shell known as the chorion. Standard cysts are typically hatched before feeding, since very young fry and shrimp larvae have limited ability to digest the unhatched shell — many other species and older larvae tolerate it without issue.
guideDecap.intro.paragraph2: Decapsulation is a chemical hydration and oxidation process that removes the outer chorion while leaving the living embryo intact in a thin membrane. This gives a higher net caloric density per gram and lets the cysts be fed directly without a separate hatching step — while Standard Cysts remain a cost-effective, widely used option for operations with established hatching infrastructure.

store.product.revive-artemia.summary: Premium-grade brine shrimp cysts engineered for consistent hatching and vigorous nauplii. High hatch rate, rich in essential fatty acids and proteins, with clean, uniform cysts that handle easily and minimise waste. Supplied in vacuum-sealed, aluminium-lined bags from 50 g to 2 kg.
store.product.revive-decapsulated-artemi: Artemia cysts with the shell fully removed, so no hatching step is required and they can be fed directly to larvae or rotifers. High in protein, lipids and essential fatty acids, and shell-free to prevent fouling and protect water quality. Vacuum-sealed, aluminium-lined bags from 50 g to 2 kg.
store.product.super-fresh-chlorella-sv-1: Premium liquid microalgae developed for intensive rotifer culture, delivering up to an 8× increase over three-day batches. High density, stable, and produced to strict biosecurity standards. Supplied ready to use in a 20-litre cold-chain insulated case.
store.product.emerald-chlorella-powder.s: Chlorella vulgaris powder produced in South Korea under controlled conditions, containing up to 97% pure Chlorella. Rich in protein, vitamins and chlorophyll, and milled fine for easy mixing into micro diets, green-water systems and rotifer culture.
store.product.vital-wheat-gluten.summary: Plant-based protein for aquafeed with a protein content typically above 82%. Works as both a nutritional component and an effective natural binder, keeping pellets durable in water without disintegrating. Suited to hatchery, grow-out and broodstock feeds.
store.product.atlantic-salmon-egg.summar: Premium-grade Atlantic salmon eggs from certified, disease-free broodstock, produced under strict biosecurity protocols and in compliance with international standards. Excellent viability, genetic integrity and predictable hatch performance for research and commercial aquaculture.
store.product.fish-meal.summary: High-protein marine ingredient from sustainably sourced whole fish and trimmings, with protein typically in the 55–65% range. Offers high digestibility and a complete amino acid profile for hatchery, grower and broodstock feeds.
store.product.seachem-stability.summary: A high-performance bacteria culture that rapidly establishes biofiltration, preventing new-tank instability and maintaining safe water conditions in both freshwater and marine systems.
